svg.font-family: -apple-system, BlinkMacSystemFont, 'Segoe UI', 'Noto Sans', Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif
svg.title: Illustrative joint distributions of digits of distinct Stoneham powers
svg.desc: Three square heat maps side by side, titled alpha against alpha squared, alpha against alpha cubed, and alpha squared against alpha cubed. Each is a 16 by 16 grid over the unit square, horizontal axis the fractional part of 2 to the n times the first power and vertical axis that of the second. Cell darkness in a single aqua hue gives the count divided by the uniform expectation 64, in five classes from below 0.8 to 1.2 or more. The shading shows no visible structure: most cells fall between 0.9 and 1.1. Below the panels: chi-square 253.7, 235.2 and 243.3 on 255 degrees of freedom, and count ratios from 0.69 to 1.44, 0.73 to 1.47, and 0.69 to 1.33. A note states that an independent uniform sample would give chi-square about 255 plus or minus 23 and that finite counts are not evidence about the limit.
svg.text: Joint digit frequencies of α, α² and α³ (finite sample)
First 4 binary digits of {2ⁿαʳ} for 0 ≤ n < 16 384; count per cell divided by the uniform 64
An independent uniform sample would give χ² ≈ 255 ± 23. Finite counts are not evidence about the limit.
Limit statement: Lean joint_uniform_powers (ST-05). Digits exact via a certified tail bound for α.
